items.definition:
to fish with a large net; to search thoroughly
They had to trawl through many documents to find the information.

to provide furniture with padding, springs, webbing, and covering
She decided to upholster the old armchair herself.

to turn into vapor
The intense heat caused the water to vaporize instantly.

manage or exploit for profit; make commercial
They decided to commercialize their new invention.

destroy or damage (metal, stone, or other materials) slowly by chemical action
Rust began to corrode the old metal pipes.

express great enthusiasm
She didn't enthuse about the idea, but she didn't reject it either.

to hypnotize or enthrall
The magician's performance seemed to mesmerise the entire audience.

to make the best or most effective use of a situation, resource, or opportunity
We need to optimise our workflow to increase efficiency.

bid higher than
They managed to outbid all other competitors for the antique.

to cause severe emotional shock and pain
The accident could traumatise him for years.

to bite or chew noisily
The horse began to chomp on the fresh hay.

to make narrower, especially by encircling pressure
The snake began to constrict its prey.

to crouch down in fear
The dog would cower under the table during thunderstorms.

to begin to grow; sprout
The seeds will germinate in a few days if kept warm and moist.

to make or become more lively or interesting
The music helped to liven up the party.

to apply a substance to minimize friction
You need to lubricate the bicycle chain regularly.

put something back together again
After cleaning, he had to reassemble the entire machine.

adjust or restore balance
Investors often rebalance their portfolios annually.

return to a former or less developed state
Without proper support, some patients may regress in their recovery.

divert from the main issue or course
Don't let yourself get sidetracked by minor details.

to cause to occur or operate at the same time or rate
We need to synchronise our watches before the mission.

say something suddenly and without careful consideration
She didn't mean to blurt out the secret.

to cause (someone) to lose confidence or hope
The defeat seemed to demoralize the entire team.

to pour a liquid over; drench; to extinguish (a fire or light)
They doused the flames with buckets of water.

to list items separately
Please itemize all your expenses on the form.

to take shape or become cohesive
The team's ideas finally started to jell after weeks of discussion.

to suffer from being forced to remain in an unpleasant place or situation
The prisoners languished in jail for years.

to value too highly
It's easy to overvalue material possessions and neglect personal relationships.

to annoy persistently
The children kept pestering their parents for ice cream.

to draw again; to change the boundaries of
They had to redraw the map after the new borders were established.

hit (someone or something) very hard
He threatened to wallop anyone who touched his car.

To make (a part of the body) sore by rubbing; to feel irritation or impatience
The rough fabric began to chafe her skin.

To officially take possession or control of (something), especially for military purposes
The police had to commandeer a civilian's car to pursue the suspect.

To provide a commentary on an event or broadcast
He was asked to commentate on the football match.

to get off (a horse, bicycle, etc.)
The rider prepared to dismount from the horse.

to make a twisted expression on one's face
He couldn't help but grimace at the bitter taste.

to confuse or bewilder
The sudden disappearance of the artifact continued to mystify experts.

to walk with exaggerated movements
The horse began to prance excitedly before the race.

to configure again or differently
We need to reconfigure the network settings for better performance.

to process again
The factory will reprocess the waste materials to extract valuable resources.

to burn with hot liquid or steam
Be careful not to scald yourself with the boiling water.

to forget or erase from one's memory something seen, especially something unpleasant
I wish I could unsee that terrible image.

to betray someone
I can't believe he would backstab his own friend.

to remove from a list, especially a stock exchange list
The company was delisted from the stock exchange.

to reproduce a message or sound in a confused, distorted way
The poor phone connection garbled the message.

stick out
The rock seemed to jut out from the cliff face.

to deal with something badly or inefficiently
The manager was criticized for mishandling the crisis.

to preserve a body by embalming and drying it
Ancient Egyptians would mummify their dead.

to classify again or differently
The library decided to reclassify some of its older books.

to invest (money) again, especially in the same enterprise
They decided to reinvest their profits in the company.

to package again or differently
The company decided to repackage its old product with a new design.

to program again or differently
The technician had to reprogram the robot's movements.

move hurriedly
Mice scurried across the floor when the light came on.

suffer from oppressive heat
We were sweltering in the humid summer heat.

present as a play or film; exaggerate
The director chose to dramatize the historical events for the film.

bend or hang downwards
The flowers began to droop after a few days without water.

to start a vehicle by connecting its battery to another vehicle's battery; to revive or accelerate something
We had to jumpstart the car this morning.

to look or gaze in an unpleasant, malicious, or lascivious way
He leered suggestively at her across the room.

to direct wrongly
The magician tried to misdirect the audience's attention.

read and mark any errors in a text
Always proofread your essays carefully before submitting them.

avoid
He tried to sidestep the question.

quarrel noisily over a trivial matter
The children often squabble over toys.

remove (someone) from a position of power or authority
The challenger hoped to unseat the incumbent mayor in the next election.

to twist and turn with quick, small movements
The worm tried to wriggle free from the hook.
